CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to evaluate the management of generalized anxiety disorder, insomnia, persistent fatigue, and tension-type headaches, with an emphasis on medication adjustments and coping strategies.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment, reporting both progress and ongoing challenges in his mental health management. He states that the sertraline 300 mg daily has contributed to a noticeable reduction in the frequency and intensity of his anxiety episodes. However, he continues to experience situational anxiety, particularly during high-pressure work deadlines. He expresses a desire to explore additional therapeutic options, including cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) sessions, to bolster his coping strategies.
His sleep quality has shown improvement since continuing trazodone at 100 mg at bedtime, with Mr. Smith noting a decrease in nocturnal awakenings. Nevertheless, he still experiences feelings of fatigue upon waking, which he attributes to residual sleep fragmentation. He is open to discussing other adjunctive treatments, such as a sleep hygiene program or melatonin dosage adjustments.
Mr. Smith reports that his tension-type headaches have remained stable in frequency, occurring about twice a week, but he notes an increase in headache intensity to 6-7 out of 10 during particularly stressful periods. He has been adhering to the ibuprofen regimen of 600 mg as needed, which provides moderate relief. He maintains a headache diary, which he finds helpful, but still struggles to pinpoint specific triggers.
Despite persistent fatigue, Mr. Smith feels that the bupropion 150 mg daily has positively influenced his energy levels and mood. He has increased his participation in physical activities, including yoga and brisk walking, which he believes have contributed to his overall well-being. However, he acknowledges occasional lapses in motivation, particularly during stressful work periods.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 300 mg daily (continued) 2. Trazodone 100 mg at bedtime (continued) 3. Lisinopril 10 mg daily (continued) 4. Ibuprofen 600 mg as needed for headache relief (continued) 5. Amitriptyline 50 mg nightly (continued) 6. Topiramate 150 mg daily (continued) 7. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (continued) 8. Melatonin 3 mg at bedtime (continued) 9. Modafinil 100 mg in the morning (continued) 10. Bupropion 150 mg daily (continued)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to engage in physical activities that support his mental health. He reports maintaining a balanced diet and has successfully reduced his caffeine intake. He participates actively in mindfulness and meditation practices, although he acknowledges that work-related stressors still present challenges to his overall well-being.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Anxiety is present but manageable; sleep quality is improved; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Headache frequency stable; intensity increased; no dizziness or visual disturbances noted. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue continues, though improved; no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 122/76 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.7F - General: Alert, oriented; appears moderately fatigued; mood appears stable with mild anxiety. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed; no tenderness in the temporal region. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable with mild anxiety.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 300 mg daily. Increase lorazepam to 1 mg twice daily as needed for acute anxiety management, with a plan to reassess in one month. Discuss referral for CBT sessions to enhance coping mechanisms. 2. Insomnia: Continue trazodone at 100 mg at bedtime, consider a trial of melatonin 5 mg if sleep quality does not improve further. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue topiramate at 150 mg daily; maintain ibuprofen at 600 mg as needed. If headache intensity increases further, consider referral to a neurologist for comprehensive evaluation. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Continue bupropion at 150 mg daily; encourage consistent physical activity and implement stress management techniques.
Follow-up appointment is scheduled for 2029-01-09 to evaluate symptom progression, medication efficacy, and address any new concerns. Mr. Smith is encouraged to continue documenting his symptoms and medication responses to facilitate ongoing management.
